sourceContext: US UI/UX design agency; this page sells senior UX strategy and advisory engagements to product leaders who need a prioritized UX roadmap.
abstract: UX consulting services give product teams senior user experience (UX) guidance through a UX maturity assessment, a product and analytics review and a prioritized UX strategy roadmap. Our UX consulting engagement takes 2–3 weeks and costs $5,000–$15,000; ongoing advisory as an embedded design team costs $15,000–$40,000 per month.

sections.answer: UX consulting is a senior advisory service that assesses how a company designs products, identifies the highest-impact UX problems and sets a prioritized plan to fix the problems. UX consultants review the product, the analytics and the design process, then score UX maturity against the Nielsen Norman Group 6-stage UX maturity model.
sections.body: UX consulting differs from UX audit services in scope: a UX audit evaluates the product interface, while UX consulting evaluates the product, the team and the process that produce the interface. A UX strategy consultant therefore delivers a roadmap for people and process as well as for screens.

sections.h2: What do UX consulting services include?
sections.answer: Our UX consulting services include 6 deliverables: stakeholder interviews, a UX maturity assessment, a product and analytics review, a UX metrics framework, a prioritized UX strategy roadmap and team coaching sessions.

items.title: Stakeholder interviews.
items.body: 6–10 interviews with product, engineering, sales and support leads set the business goals, for example a 45-minute session with the head of product.

items.title: UX maturity assessment.
items.body: The design process is scored against the Nielsen Norman Group UX maturity model and the human-centred design activities of ISO 9241-210, for example research frequency and design-system adoption.

items.title: Product and analytics review.
items.body: Key flows are reviewed against usability heuristics and Google Analytics 4 funnels, for example onboarding completion and checkout drop-off.

items.title: UX metrics framework.
items.body: Goals, signals and metrics are defined with the Google HEART framework (happiness, engagement, adoption, retention and task success), for example an activation rate target for onboarding.

items.title: Prioritized UX strategy roadmap.
items.body: Initiatives are ranked with RICE prioritization (reach, impact, confidence and effort), for example a quarter-by-quarter plan of research and design work.

items.title: Team coaching sessions.
items.body: Designers and product managers receive 4–6 working sessions on methods, for example Double Diamond discovery and Jobs to be Done interviews.

sections.h2: How does the UX consulting process work?
sections.answer: The UX consulting process takes 2–3 weeks (10–15 working days) and runs in 4 steps, from stakeholder interviews to the roadmap workshop.

items.title: Stakeholder interviews (2–3 days)
items.body: We interview 6–10 leads, collect business goals and receive analytics and product access.

items.title: Product and process review (4–6 days)
items.body: A senior UX consultant reviews key flows, analytics funnels, research history and the design workflow.

items.title: Maturity scoring and strategy (2–4 days)
items.body: Findings are scored on the UX maturity model and turned into initiatives with RICE scores and HEART metrics.

items.title: Roadmap workshop (2 days)
items.body: We present the UX strategy roadmap in a 2-hour workshop and agree owners and dates for each initiative.

sections.h2: What are the benefits of UX consulting?
sections.answer: UX consulting has 4 benefits: UX consulting increases activation rate, improves team UX skills, reduces rework cost and develops UX maturity.

items.title: Increases activation rate
items.body: Fixing the onboarding and first-use problems found in the product review increases the share of new users who reach the first key action.

items.title: Improves team UX skills
items.body: Coaching sessions improve how designers and product managers run research, design critiques and prioritization.

items.title: Reduces rework cost
items.body: Validating product direction before development reduces the design and engineering days spent rebuilding shipped features.

items.title: Develops UX maturity
items.body: Quarterly roadmap reviews develop the company's UX maturity one stage at a time on the Nielsen Norman Group model.

sections.h2: Which types of UX consulting do we offer?
sections.answer: Our UX consulting services come in 4 types: strategy for a live product, pre-build UX strategy, artificial intelligence (AI) feature advisory and ongoing advisory; accessibility reviews run through our UX audit.

items.title: UX strategy and consulting for a live product.
items.body: The core UX consulting service: stakeholder interviews, a product and analytics review and a prioritized roadmap in 2–3 weeks, for example when retention stalls and nobody can name the cause.

items.title: Pre-build UX strategy.
items.body: Before leadership funds design work on a new product line, the engagement sets UX goals, HEART metrics and a roadmap, so the first design sprint starts from agreed priorities.

items.title: AI feature advisory.
items.body: For an AI feature, the product review checks trust (how users know the AI is right), transparency (what the system is doing) and actionability (what the user does next).

items.title: Ongoing UX advisory.
items.body: After the roadmap, advisory continues as an embedded design team at $15,000–$40,000 per month, with weekly sessions and quarterly roadmap reviews that track UX maturity.

items.title: Accessibility review through our UX audit.
items.body: Accessibility questions go to our UX audit, which checks audited screens against Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 level AA; a full-site accessibility audit is quoted separately.

sections.answer: UX consulting sets strategy for the product, the team and the design process; a UX audit evaluates the product interface only. Companies start with UX consulting if no UX plan exists, and start with a UX audit if the interface problem is already known. If you go the audit route, our guide on choosing between a UX audit agency, a freelancer or an AI tool shows what each provider type finds.

sections.h2: How much does UX consulting cost?
sections.answer: UX consulting costs $5,000–$15,000 and takes 2–3 weeks. The price depends on 4 factors: the number of products, the number of stakeholder interviews, the number of teams coached and the need for ongoing advisory.
sections.body: A UX strategy engagement for 1 product with 6 stakeholder interviews sits near $5,000. An engagement for 3 products, 10 stakeholder interviews and 2 coached teams sits near $15,000. Ongoing UX advisory continues as an embedded design team at $15,000–$40,000 per month, and teams that need new user evidence add UX research services.

sections.h2: When should a leadership team hire UX consulting services?
sections.answer: A leadership team should hire UX consulting services in 5 situations:
items: Product decisions rely on opinion, if the company has no UX research or UX metrics.
A company builds a first design team, if no senior designer sets the design process.
Activation rate or retention stalls, if the product team cannot name the cause.
A new product line starts, if leadership needs a UX strategy before funding design work.
Design and engineering disagree on priorities, if the backlog has no shared scoring method.

sections.h2: What should you look for in a UX consulting company?
sections.answer: Look for a UX consulting company that names its senior lead, works from evidence, scores every recommendation and fixes scope and price in writing. Use these 8 checks to compare UX consultants:
items: A named senior lead, because the person who runs the stakeholder interviews and the roadmap workshop sets the quality of the plan; ask who that is before you sign.
A published maturity model, so a good UI UX consultant scores your team against the Nielsen Norman Group UX maturity model now and again next quarter.

Evidence before opinion: expect requests for analytics access, Google Analytics 4 funnels and past user research such as personas or journey maps in the first days, because advice without evidence is a guess.
A scoring method such as RICE prioritization, so design and engineering agree on the order of work instead of arguing over it.
A metric for every initiative, for example an activation rate target from the Google HEART framework, so you can tell whether a fix worked.

Coaching that stays with your team, because a fixed-scope UX consulting engagement ends after a few weeks; working sessions on methods such as Jobs to be Done interviews let the team run the roadmap alone.
A fixed scope and price in writing, so deliverables, weeks and cost cannot drift; every project with us begins with a free consultation and a fixed-scope proposal.
Case studies that explain decisions, because screens alone show design skill; ask for one project where discovery shaped the product strategy.

sections.h2: What does UX consulting look like on a real project?
sections.answer: Our Mass Media Co. project was a product revamp, not a UX consulting engagement, but it opened with consulting-style discovery: a workshop that aligned strategy with business goals.
sections.body: Mass Media Co. ran order taking across separate systems. The Mass Media Co. case study describes a discovery workshop with stakeholders and users that aligned the revamp strategy with business goals and covered product definition, strategy, information architecture and user flows. The whole revamp reported a 30% increase in order processing efficiency, so credit that figure to the full project. Ask any UX consulting company for a case like this.

sections.answer: These answers cover what UX consultants do, what the work costs and takes, how it differs from audits and design, AI, and fit for startups and remote teams.

faqs.q: What does a UX consultant do?
faqs.a: A UX consultant assesses a product, the product team and the design process, then delivers a prioritized UX strategy roadmap and coaches the team to execute the roadmap. UX consultants advise rather than design, so screen work is quoted as a design sprint or a full design engagement.

UX stands for user experience, meaning every interaction a person has with a product, from sign-up to getting support. User experience design consulting improves it by changing the priorities, metrics and team habits behind those interactions. Our product review also checks the user interface (UI), the screens and controls users touch, in each key flow, so UI consulting services start from the same review.

faqs.q: Is UX consulting different from a UX audit?
faqs.a: Yes. UX consulting covers strategy, team process and UX maturity, while a UX audit covers only the usability issues in the product interface. Teams that need both can book them as one sequence, and the audit's fix roadmap then becomes an input to the UX strategy roadmap.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to hire a UX designer?
faqs.a: Hiring UX designers through our agency costs $5,000–$180,000 per project, or $15,000–$40,000 per month for an embedded team of 2–5 designers. UX consulting with a senior UX consultant and a UX audit with 1–2 designers each cost $5,000–$15,000 over 2–3 weeks, a research and UX design sprint with 2–4 designers costs $25,000–$60,000 over 4–8 weeks, and full design with a design system runs $60,000–$180,000 over 8–16 weeks with 3–6 designers.

faqs.q: Is UX consulting worth it for startups?
faqs.a: Yes, for a startup with a live product whose activation rate or retention has stalled without a clear cause, because an engagement for 1 product and 6 stakeholder interviews sits near $5,000 and names the fixes first. A startup without a product yet gets more from UI UX design for startups, which validates a minimum viable product (MVP) in 4–8 weeks.

faqs.q: Can UX consulting be done remotely?
faqs.a: Yes. We deliver UX consulting services remote-first to product teams across the United States from our headquarters in Reston, Virginia, so the stakeholder interviews, the product and analytics review and the roadmap workshop can run without an on-site visit. Your team shares product and analytics access in the first 2–3 days, during the stakeholder interview step.

faqs.q: Is UX at risk from AI?
faqs.a: No. We use AI to accelerate production work, but the judgment about what to design still comes from research with real users and pattern recognition across 200+ products. AI features add UX work rather than remove it, because users need to trust the output, see what the system is doing and know what to do next.
Yes. Ongoing UX consulting runs as an embedded design team at $15,000–$40,000 per month, with weekly advisory sessions and quarterly roadmap reviews.

faqs.q: Does UX consulting include design work?
faqs.a: No. UX consulting delivers a UX strategy, a UX metrics framework and a roadmap; interface design work is quoted as a design sprint or a full design engagement.

faqs.q: How long does UX consulting take?
faqs.a: UX consulting takes 2–3 weeks, which equals 10–15 working days, from the first stakeholder interview to the roadmap workshop.
